text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
JOSEPH-NICEPHORE NIEPCE, French chemist and pioneer in photography, was born in 1765. He is said to have produced a photograph on metal, the world's first.
English artist SIR EDWARD LANDSEER, a favourite of QUEEN VICTORIA and PRINCE ALBERT, was born in 1802.
Polish ornthologist GRACIUS BROINOWSKI, who literally "jumped ship" and swan ashore at Portland in Victoria to become a publisher ofbooks on Australian birds, was born in 1837.
Australian racehorse breeder ROBERT TOWN, whose American stallion "CHILDE HAROLD" is remembered in the name of the Sydney racetrack Harold Park, was born in 1840.
French composer MAURICE RAVEL, best known for "BOLERO", was born in 1875.
Antiguan cricketer known as the "Master Blaster", VIV RICHARDS, was born on this day in 1952.

British comedian who found fame in 'THE YOUNG ONES', RICK MAYALL, was born in 1958. Another television series in which he used his comic talents was "Bottom" and he starred in the movie "Drop Dead Fred".
Czechoslovakian-born American tennis professional IVAN LENDL was born in 1960.

US singer TAYLOR DAYNE (LESLEY WONDERMAN) was born in 1962. She started her career as a dancer and then joined a heavy metal group before going solo. Her hits included "Tell It To My Heart" (1987), "I'll Always Love You" (1988), "Don't Rush Me" (1988) and "With Every Beat Of My Heart" (1989).
** EVENTS **
1836 : Surveyer-General ROBERT HODDLE laid out the main
streets of Melbourne.
1838 : Famous operatic soprano JENNY LIND, known as the
"Swedish Nightingale", made her debut.
1876 : ALEXANDER GRAHAM BELL was issued with a patent
for the telephone, after filing for the patent 3 weeks earlier.
1912 : French aviator HENRI SEIMET flew from Paris to
London in 3 hours, the first person to complete the route non-stop.
1917 : The world's first jazz record, "The Dixieland Jazz
Band One Step", recorded by NICK LaROCCA's Original Dixieland Jazz Band, was released by RCA Victor in Camden, N.J.
1936 : In contempt of the Versailles Treaty imposed after
the First World War, ADOLF HITLER marched his troops into the demilitarised zone East of the Rhine River, bringing calls of action from France.
1945 : Nine years to the day since HITLER's troops took
the Rhineland, American forces seized the strategic bridge over the Rhine at Remagen and began crossing into Germany.
1960 : The United States and the Soviet Union offered to
protect all weaker nations of the world against nuclear attack.
1971 : Swiss women were finally given the right to vote
and hold Federal office.
1989 : A convicted murderer in South Carolina, who
successfully appealed against being sent to the electric chair, was accidentally electrocuted while sitting on a prison-toilet mending a pair of earphones.
1989 : Chinese security forces opened fire on Tibetan
monks and civilians in Lhasa, killing 12 people. The Chinese were cracking-down on demonstrations, calling for independence from China.
1994 : Adelaide winemaker MAX SCHUBERT, the creater of
the famous Grange Hermitage, died at the age of 79.
1994 : A second strain of the HIV virus was detected in
Victoria, with two men diagnosed as being infected with HIV-2.
1996 : Three U.S. servicemen were jailed in Japan for up
to seven years for the abduction and rape of an Okinawa schoolgirl in 1995.
